spans.text: Smack! Smack!
The camera shakes violently.
There is a faint electrical hum as the screen slowly brightens, and the rumbling in the background grows louder.
Hello, hello? Is this piece of crap on?
Do you read me? One-two-three-four-five-six-seven, pathetic maggots of Griffin?
Smack! Smack!
Dreamer continues brutalizing the device.
Quit hitting it! It's recording!
Everything we say and do is going to be preserved for the Commander!
Seriously, you guys... Could you make some room and not block the platform in the background?
Let's hurry up and deal with the mission here. There's more good stuff inside the tower.
Oh dear, I'm sorry.
Go ahead, Team Leader Judge.
Ahem. Everyone, pay attention.
Commander, this is the combat log of Team Fe56-C.
Our current location is the Avernus platform.
Mission progress—all active forces on the platform including Narciss have been subdued. Daybreak has entered the Eastern Tower, and they're beginning the signal search assignment.
Now commencing sensitive site exploitation.
Beep.

On the outskirts of Avernus. The rain here is light and intermittent.
Shellfire washes across the landscape, scattering blades, armor plates, shell casings, severed limbs, and white-colored debris in its wake.
The brightest point in the dark night is a blazing fire that belches thick black clouds of acrid smoke.

An overturned truck burns merrily and the body of a white-armored trooper hangs out the side. It looks like it was trying to flee, but it has been burned to a blackened crisp that hangs forlornly over the door frame.
That's... Team D's chopper!
There's a helicopter not too far off. Its logo has been repainted, and it's half-buried in the dirt. Its tail rotor has been broken off and is nowhere in sight.
Ahahaha, Intruder got jammed by the radiation, and her chopper crashed; what a joke!
I hope it keeps raining. I'll take a nice memorial photo for you.
Hey!
The fine droplets fall in sheets as they splash into the ground. This rain comes from the sky above Avernus, or more specifically, from the Collapse particle clouds.
Even the mechanical bodies of Dolls and S.F. units won't survive prolonged exposure to such conditions.
The camera wobbles and focuses on a point in the distance.
The searchlight on the watchtower was extinguished before the fighting started, and now it stands as a pitch-black monolith in the distance.
Solidified Collapse radiation crystals stud the surrounding black rocks.
Huh, we've got more visibility now. Take a look...
It hasn't improved much. This rain won't let up for quite a while.
Let's move on to the next location.
On the edge of the Avernus platform.
A large fleet of aircraft is vital to keeping Avernus connected to the external watchtowers. Naturally, the aircraft landing pads are also designated as a vital region.
The entire platform is supported by a metal framework, and intricate white indicator lines crisscross on its surface, designating different parking areas.
It's not unthinkable for there to be several dozen craft parked here during the busiest times.
Right now, however, the only things here besides several largely intact aircraft are scattered hunks of metallic wreckage, engines, and glass shards...
The captives have been disarmed and are currently gathered inside a landing pad, not daring to raise their heads.
Ha, I remember now! We hacked those two aircraft in the distance before they could take off.
I personally blew up this one here, knocked its doors right off, hahahaha...
In the distance, the hitherto quiescent aircraft that Dreamer is pointing to begins to wobble and creak.
Huh? Why is it moving?
Nytos! Take cover!
...The camera shakes violently.
However, the expected sound of gunfire does not come.
The fragile aircraft tilts forward like a broken seesaw.
A black mechanical arm holding a massive gun emerges slowly from the rear seat.
A Nyto drags her ruined body out of the cabin and pulls the trigger in a frenzy...
Click, click, click.
...Oh dear, ammo problem, cutie?
Maggots... must be... cleansed...
This is... Big Sister's order!
...Bang-bang-bang!
Alchemist fires off several shots and the struggling Nyto stops moving.
Glass shards tinkle as they fall to the ground, refracting the faint light accompanying this drizzle.
Tsk, when will they learn?
Let's sweep the platform again just in case more rats come out.
Stacks of supply crates line the side of the platform. It seems they weren't moved away in time.
There is a metal door at the base of the steps opposite them.
Destroyer reaches out to push it. It gives way and she almost falls in.
Dammit, I thought it was locked!
Don't wreck the scene.
We'll head down to check it out after we finish checking the platform.
There is an ordinary-looking truck covered in bullet holes. It was clearly used as cover during a previous firefight.
Some of its cargo still hasn't been loaded yet. Among them, a cardboard box was ripped open by a powerful impact, revealing a white statue of a woman.
This statue holds an Epiphyllum in its hand, and there is a mysterious smile on its face. That smile seems... somewhat familiar.
So this is the kind of junk that Paradeus uses to trick their followers?
When humans have nothing else to place their faith in, they will cling to anything, even a stalk of grass.
The radiation levels here are very high, and they're even higher in the vehicle.
Alchemist slices open a row of boxes with a swipe of her hand, and a huge pile of spherical objects spills out.
According to our intel and the radiation scans, these are the "Boxes of Iaso" produced by Paradeus. They should be glowing.
The spheres are smaller than the dimensions listed by the database, and more portable, too.
Ah, I know why they aren't glowing.
Alchemist fiddles with one, then savagely rips it open... revealing nothing inside the box.
By the looks of the scene, Paradeus probably destroyed this cargo... but why didn't they ship it away or just dump it?
Who cares about looking at a bunch of junk? Let's move on to the next location.
